memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: "For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power and of love and of a sound mind." —  (2 Timothy 1:7)

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
Abraham Lincoln is often cited as a leader who possessed a "holy common sense." Like the qualities E. Stanley Jones admired, Lincoln was a man of profound candour and courtesy. He led a divided nation not just through political maneuvering, but through a spiritual groundedness in the Bible. He understood that the "jewels" of the Sermon on the Mount were not just for the pulpit, but for the presidency. His common sense told him that "a house divided against itself cannot stand," a truth rooted deeply in the words of Christ.

We often over-complicate our faith with rituals, yet Lincoln showed that true spirituality is found in the simple, sensible application of justice and mercy. He had the candour to face the horror of slavery and the courtesy to treat his enemies with grace. If we meditate on God's Word but fail to use the "sound mind" He gave us to solve the problems of our neighbors, our faith remains hollow. Common sense is the bridge between our silent prayers and our public impact. Let us stop waiting for a miraculous sign to do what is obviously right, and instead, use the wisdom God has already placed within us to heal our nation.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: "I am not bound to win, but I am bound to be true. I am not bound to succeed, but I am bound to live up to what light I have." — Abraham Lincoln

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, grant us the gift of holy common sense. Help us, like Lincoln, to be people of unwavering candour and Christ-like courtesy. Give us a sound mind to discern the truth and the practical wisdom to live it out in our homes, our workplaces, and our nation. Let our faith be seen not just in our words, but in our simple, sensible acts of honesty and mercy. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Don't wait for a grand revelation to do what is right. Use the "common sense" God gave you to be a blessing today sometimes the most spiritual thing you can do is simply be sensible, kind, and truthful.
